title: Non-Atomic Compound Check-Then-Act
pattern: A sequence where a thread reads shared state to verify a condition, then performs a write based on that condition, without acquiring an exclusive lock across both operations.
why_bad: Between the check phase and the act phase, another thread can interleave and modify the shared state, rendering the initial check invalid and causing race conditions or duplicate insertions [24:211].
detection: A check-then-act sequence performed on concurrent/synchronized collections or shared variables that does not reside within a single atomic lock guard or atomic compare-and-swap loop [24:211].
fix: Enclose the check-then-act sequence within a mutual exclusion lock to guarantee atomicity [24:211].
